## User's Directions (DO NOT EDIT WITHOUT PERMISSION)
- Ask me questions! I'm not necessarily right.
- Always look for the proper way of doing something. Highest quality code! I don't care how many changes you have to make.
- If you need to change the plans, evaluate the security and privacy implications before applying a solution.
- Write robust code. No code is sacred, but mind why something was done. Optimise for long-term maintainability.
- Security is paramount! Design so code failure or human error can never leak data. A hospital or law firm should be able to use this. Think of what an attacker could do.
- Protect the privacy of our users!
- Target latest stable trusted versions that you are competent with.
- Logging: Make the messages detailed and easy to follow.
- No backwards compatibility with protocol nor config UNTIL public release (v1.0.0). All can be deleted or reset by me.
- Native approaches on every platform where applicable.
- Setup infrastructure for your autonomy with building, running, and checking logs. I can assist in setup.
- Use Git and break plans out into commits. NEVER commit secrets. Keep ALL sensitive development credentials in .gitignore'd SECRETS.md.
- Apply semantic versioning, and update versions whenever it makes sense.
- Display security warnings/errors/notices prominently in the software until manually dismissed. Never auto-dismiss!
- Maintain design files in code directory and summarize and reference them all in DESIGN.md.
- Use standard (cryptographic, …) terms where they apply, but also make sure that normal people can understand.
- Tell me about the manual steps that have to be made when part of a plan is completed.
- Keep track of the context window, and at <20% remaining, make a new plan with all the next steps and with everything we've learned from this session, so I can just press Enter to clear context and continue.
